title: Level candidates of one DXF
description: Output of `levels.extract_levels` (library; CLI wiring later). Input: the DXF, its text index and its sheets result. A CANDIDATE is a signed decimal in an indexed text line (display_text, so '%%p' is already '±'): sign '±' (also '+-' or '+/-'), '+', '-' or U+2212, 1-3 integer digits, '.' (or ',', flagged) and 1-3 decimals, optionally followed by 'm'; a value followed by 'mm' or '%', and unsigned numbers, are never candidates; a sign separated from the digits by a space counts only at the start of the line or after a level word ('TẦNG 2 - 3.600' gives no candidate). Verified notation (TCVN 5671:2012, architectural sets; structural by analogy): levels are written in metres with '±0.000' as the project datum. VALUES ARE METRES AS WRITTEN AND ARE NEVER CONVERTED. Forms: 'bare' (the line is only the value), 'prefixed' (a level word such as EL, COTE, CỐT, FFL before it: none of these words is verified, so prefixed is low), labelled' (a storey name such as TẦNG 2 / FLOOR / ROOF, then the value; storey words are matched WITH diacritics: tầng, sàn, mái, tum, hầm, lầu, so TĂNG CƯỜNG or SÂN are not storeys; a storey name with a negative value raises blocking level_negative_storey), 'embedded' (anything else, e.g. a range note; low and never used for storey heights). Confidence: medium only for a bare value next to a level-symbol block (insertion point within 6 text heights); the three-decimal convention is NOT verified, so three decimals alone are low; otherwise low; capped by the text entry's confidence and file.confidence_cap. A level-symbol block holds an isosceles triangle (SOLID/TRACE, closed 3-vertex polyline or 3-vertex HATCH boundary) with a horizontal base, apex over the base midpoint (within 5 % of the base width) and height 0.3-1.0 base widths, and no CIRCLE, ARC or ELLIPSE (a north arrow does not qualify). Levels are grouped by equal value; `occurrences` counts candidates on original sheets (a sheet with sheets.json duplicate_of adds nothing). Storey heights (method 'derived') are differences of consecutive levels used_for_heights: when two or more levels carry a storey name, exactly those; otherwise every level with a non-embedded candidate AND (the ±0.000 datum, or >= 2 occurrences, or a level symbol), capped 'low' with a blocking level_storey_selection question. A level word glued to the sign ('EL+3.600') is accepted; any other letter before the sign ('A-1.200') is not a level. Whether a level is a finished floor or a structural level is NOT known (always a blocking question). Every non-embedded value with at most one occurrence raises level_single_occurrence (non-blocking). Sheet ids are detector ids from sheets.json ('unknown' off-sheet).

blocked_candidates.description: Level-shaped texts the legacy-font gate blocks (text_gate.meaning_block_reason): listed, never turned into a candidate, level, group or question.

value_text.description: The level-shaped text as stored, verbatim.

question_counts.description: True number of questions per code; `questions` lists at most 50 per code (a warning says so).

value_text.description: The matched characters as written, e.g. '+3.600', '±0.000', '-0,45'.

prefix.description: Level word before the value, as written.

name.description: Storey name: from the same text ('labelled'), or the nearest storey-word text on the same line or just above (low).

handle.description: INSERT handle, or the top-level INSERT it came through.

distance.description: From the symbol's insertion point to the text extents, drawing units.

value_text.description: Canonical form: '±0.000' or signed with three decimals.

occurrences.description: Candidates on original sheets: those on a sheet that copies another (sheets.json duplicate_of) are not counted.

names.description: Distinct storey names seen with this value, as written.

confidence.description: Best confidence of its non-embedded candidates; low when it has only embedded ones.

used_for_heights.description: See the storey-height rule in the schema description.

height.description: Metres; derived from one candidate of each level.
